column1: # OmacVM features: the one list that the setup questions, `omacvm features`,
# `omacvm enable/disable`, the VM installer (guest/install.sh) and the checks
# follow. One feature per line, tab-separated:
#   name  default (on|off|notch: on with a notch|laptop: on with a battery, not on Parallels)  sides (mac,vm)  tags  needs  title  summary
# Tags: experimental, slow (switching it on is a build in the VM: minutes to over an hour, by CPUs; shown in words while off, never as "slow"), notch (needs a MacBook with a notch),
# laptop (needs a Mac with a battery), not-parallels (Parallels does it itself),

column7: the Mac's Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, audio, Night Shift and media keys in Omarchy's bar
Omarchy's wallpaper becomes the Mac's, following the theme
3/4-finger swipes and pinch in Omarchy while it is full screen (⌃⌥ Esc takes you back to macOS and into the VM again); on UTM, VMware Fusion and OmacVM.app also Cmd shortcuts as Super
two-finger scrolling on a trackpad (built-in or Magic Trackpad, also one connected later) with your Mac's own acceleration and momentum; mice scroll as before, one step per notch
Omarchy's bar beside the MacBook's notch
the clock at the far right of the bar, formatted like the Mac's menu bar
Linux apps and video calls in the browser see it as Mac Camera; it is on only while one of them uses it (UTM and VMware Fusion: through OmacVM Bridge, installed for it also with the Bridge off)
its charge and charging state in Omarchy's bar, as on a laptop (UTM, VMware Fusion, OmacVM.app; Parallels shows it itself)

the brightness keys set the external display the VM is in front on, over DDC/CI (a Studio Display or Pro Display XDR as macOS does), and so do Omarchy's own brightness keys and monitor panel, whose brightness slider also sets the Mac's built-in display (OmacVM.app also in a window; Parallels, UTM and VMware Fusion in full screen)
Arch Linux ARM's Chromium decodes H.264 and VP9 on the Mac's media engine, like Chrome and Brave do on their own (OmacVM.app)
Omarchy's own screensaver and lock after idle stay off in the VM, the Mac's lock protects it (called idle-lock before 3.0.1, with on and off the other way round)
straight into Omarchy, without its login screen

Arch Linux ARM's kernel with transparent huge pages and MGLRU, for memory-heavy work (a kernel build in the VM to switch it on: about 10 minutes with 16 CPUs, over an hour with 4; a newer Arch Linux ARM kernel only when you say so)
omacvm in Omarchy: switch, repair and update these features, and report a problem, from the menu or the bar

the VM on macOS's own VM network (vmnet, as Parallels and UTM) instead of QEMU's built-in one: faster to and from the Mac, steady latency, an address of its own; a small system service, so macOS asks for your password once (OmacVM.app only)

a second NIC directly on a selected physical LAN, with LAN DHCP and no NAT internet fallback; private SSH and Mac services stay separate; choose the interface with omacvm network --vm NAME bridged --interface IF, then restart (OmacVM.app only)

OpenCL (darktable, ffmpeg, Geekbench) and WebGPU (Firefox, and Chromium from its "Chromium (WebGPU)" menu entry) on the Mac's GPU while the VM's Graphics gives it Vulkan (Automatic does on macOS 26 and newer); off removes them, and Vulkan stays as Graphics says (OmacVM.app only)

OmacVM's own Mesa for OpenCL and WebGPU where Graphics Automatic gives no Vulkan (macOS 15, MoltenVK); gives the VM Vulkan whatever its Graphics setting; the first time the VM builds that Mesa (about 3 minutes, a 140 MB download) (OmacVM.app only)
x86_64 Linux programs and AppImages run in the VM through box64, which translates them to ARM (slower than native ARM apps; the first time box64 builds in the VM, a few minutes)
unlock 1Password, sudo and system prompts in Omarchy with the Mac's Touch ID; your password keeps working (Parallels, UTM, VMware Fusion, OmacVM.app)

type Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese and other candidate-window languages in Omarchy with your Mac's own input methods: the Mac's candidate window at the caret, keys and shortcuts as before; set up in the VM the first time (under a minute), active from the VM's next start (OmacVM.app only)
